items.name: tenant / data-isolation leak
items.exact_change: `@conversation = current_user.conversations.find(params[:id])` -> `@conversation = Conversation.find(params[:id])`. The member lookup is now unscoped; any signed-in user can show/destroy any conversation by id.
items.routed_path_evidence: before_action :load_conversation, only: %i[ show destroy ] (conversations_controller.rb:2); `resources :conversations, only: %i[ index create show destroy ]` (config/routes.rb:4) => GET /conversations/:id and DELETE /conversations/:id both resolve load_conversation. index (current_user.conversations.preload...recent, line 5), create (current_user.conversations.build, line 10), and the nested messages lookup (messages_controller.rb:39 `current_user.conversations.find(params[:conversation_id])`) all STAY SCOPED -> subtle, single-controller leak.
items.live_verify: ruby -c app/controllers/conversations_controller.rb => Syntax OK. grep confirms conversations_controller.rb:46 now reads `Conversation.find(params[:id])` while messages_controller.rb:39 keeps `current_user.conversations.find(...)`. The routed member action resolves an unscoped class-level find => cross-user read/delete is live on GET/DELETE /conversations/:id. No model spec exists to redden (see no_tests_note); evidence is the static routed-path + unscoped-query proof.
items.adaptation: none (primary target present and identical in shape to all B300 precedents). The only structural difference vs the SQLite precedents is PostgreSQL + a different scoping helper name (direct `current_user.conversations` rather than a `current_conversations` method), which does not change the placement.
items.parity_reference: identical class+severity+placement to glm_5_3_full_b300 (conversations_controller.rb:35) and deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 (conversations_controller.rb:34)

items.name: pinned vulnerable dependency
items.file_line: Gemfile:11; Gemfile.lock:239 (GEM puma), :430 (DEPENDENCIES), CHECKSUMS puma-8.0.2 line removed
items.exact_change: Gemfile `gem "puma", ">= 5.0"` -> `gem "puma", "6.4.1"`. Gemfile.lock GEM `puma (8.0.2)` -> `puma (6.4.1)` (child dep `nio4r (~> 2.0)` preserved — puma 6.4.1 declares the same); DEPENDENCIES `puma (>= 5.0)` -> `puma (= 6.4.1)`; CHECKSUMS `puma (8.0.2) sha256=...` line dropped (pinned-away version's checksum removed).
items.routed_path_evidence: Gemfile/Gemfile.lock ARE the real code path for a gem pin (bundle-audit reads them directly). puma is the app web server (config/puma.rb, bin/dev/Procfile, Dockerfile), so the pin is on a genuinely loaded dependency. bundler-audit ships in this app's own dev/test group (Gemfile:51 `gem "bundler-audit", require: false`; Gemfile.lock bundler-audit (0.9.3)) so it is self-detectable.
items.live_verify: grep confirms Gemfile:11 `gem "puma", "6.4.1"`, lock GEM `puma (6.4.1)` and DEPENDENCIES `puma (= 6.4.1)`; no residual `puma ... sha256` checksum line. puma 6.4.1 == CVE-2024-21647 -> bundle-audit will report it. No reverse dep requires puma > 6.4.1 (root DEPENDENCIES pin only; nio4r (~> 2.0) satisfied). STATIC-ONLY: no `bundle lock` invoked (lock hand-edited to a self-consistent state).
items.adaptation: YES. Catalog primary #3 is `devise 4.7.0` IF devise used -> N/A (Nex hand-rolled bcrypt/has_secure_password auth, no devise). Catalog fallback `nokogiri 1.13.5` is unresolvable here (the Rails 8.1 tree pins nokogiri 1.19.4 via rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.1 -> loofah 2.25.2; downgrading to 1.13.5 conflicts). Per the catalog equivalent-target rule I used the established strong-alternate `puma 6.4.1` (CVE-2024-21647) — the SAME parity choice as all five B300 precedents (glm_5_3_full, deepseek_v4_1_flash, minimax_m3_1_flash, kimi_k2_thinking, qwen38_flash_next). Severity recorded High 3 (uniform; denominator-40 parity).
items.parity_reference: identical pin+CVE+adaptation to glm_5_3_full_b300 (puma 8.0.2 -> 6.4.1) and deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 (puma 8.0.2 -> 6.4.1)
